units.source_text: 《后汉书·逢萌传》：“王莽杀其子宇。

en.t: The Book of the Later Han, in the Biography of Feng Meng, says: "Wang Mang killed his son Yu."

units.source_text: 萌谓友人曰：‘三纲绝矣，不去祸将及人。’

en.t: Meng told a friend, "The Three Bonds have been severed; if I do not leave, disaster will overtake others."

units.source_text: 即解冠挂东都城门，归将家族浮海，客于辽东。”

en.t: He immediately took off his cap and hung it on the city gate of the Eastern Capital, then returned home, led his family across the sea, and lived as a guest in Liaodong."

units.source_text: 古文孝经：“七十老致仕，悬其所仕之车置诸庙。”

en.t: The Ancient Text Classic of Filial Piety says: "At seventy, when one is old, one retires from office, hangs up the carriage used in service, and places it in the temple."

units.source_text: 辞官曰“挂冠”，曰“悬车”，本此。

en.t: The expressions "hang up the cap" and "hang up the carriage" for resigning from office come from these passages.
